questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Interesting professors, outdoors recreation and regional interest

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great, one course was less interesting, and I would have liked to live on campus.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I knew most

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: One introduction event - it was not very good.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think I could have gone there and gotten help, but I did not.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: easy, took 2 days. I found it in a facebook group and drove there on bicycle. I paid the same as the on campus residents.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: UBC have great housing for exchange students and it is cheap, you are missing out on some social stuff by living off campus. Off campus housing is less noisy and probably more clean. It is easy to get around in Vancouver with public transport or bicycle.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think the UBC housing was alright. I liked the place I lived off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a lot of information about the courses, I recommend taking a lot of courses and the dropping some.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You fill out a form, and they assign you courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: email and consultation. Thay also send a lot of reminders and did a zoom meeting about it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I did well, but I should maybe have gotten one more advanced course instead of one of the courses I got.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: register 4-5 courses and then drop out in the first weeks. Also consider changing in the first week. 5 or more courses a probably too much.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did two fourth year couses and one 3rd year course. Fourth year courses was with a lot of academic writing and research oriented. The 3rd year course had some mandatory ethics and was in general easy and a bit boring.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of variation between the courses, difficult to say if there were big differences. The pace was in general faster and more students were active. They use "canvas" like we do. There were more assignment during the courses and some of them were very small.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Indigenous Forestry (3rd year)
Human-Wildlife conflict management (4th year)
Plant Ecology (4th year)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Plant Ecology was really good, it is a mix of lectures and group work and you write a scientific paper together in the group, you also get a good introduction to R and the course also had small ongoing written exercises about academic diversity and minorities in academia.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used more on my bicycle than expected. But I had fun with repairing it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Food was more expensive than I thought it would be. Nothing was less expensive.
But you can save money by being part of clubs to borrow cheap or free gear.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good but overwhelming. Not easy to decide and know how to engage.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: everything

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The varcity outdoor club. Get there early and ask how you participate. 

The "coconut party" with the forestry department.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the gulf islands for kayaking and biking . Buy or rent a good bicycle and go around town. Go climbing in Squarmish.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, everyone is very helpful.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Clubs and try find some friends in class. Okay to only socialize with other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: people are very open and sometimes superficial - it helps with meeting new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Get some social life - try find some other exchange student in your course - consider changing courses if you only have very big ones.
2. Use the beanery in fairview crescent - it is a good hang out spot.
3. If you want to get into a club or do a sport, then decide fast, because the applications are early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: This is a good university, and the professors are very friendly and more accessible. Use it :)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Good courses, I got much better at R and I learned a lot. I liked living in another place, and knowing that I could do everything on my own.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: loneliness in the first months, especially the lack of hugs. I didn't know anyone well and I missed my girlfriend, family and friends, but it was manageable and also empowering.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is very nice to have someone come visit: a friend, family or girlfriend.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
